title: Chicken pot pie soup with biscuits
equipment: 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven or soup pot

items: Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Heat the oven to the temperature on the biscuit package (usually 350°F) with a rack in the middle. Set the biscuits 2 inches apart on a baking sheet.
Melt the butter in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6–8 min, stirring often, until the onion is soft and see-through. Stir in the garlic for 30 sec.
Put the biscuits in the oven and bake as the package says, usually 13–17 min, until deep golden brown.
While they bake, sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly 1 min, until no dry flour shows.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk, so no lumps form. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then lower to medium-low and simmer 10 min, stirring often, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the chicken, peas and thyme. Simmer 3–5 min, until the chicken is hot and the peas are bright green. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and set a warm biscuit on top of each.
tips: Keep it at a gentle simmer once the milk is in. A hard boil can make it separate.
No rotisserie chicken? Simmer 1 lb boneless chicken breast in the broth 15–20 min, until it reads 165°F, then shred it and use the broth in the soup.
For a heartier soup, add 1 diced Yukon Gold potato with the carrots and simmer until fork-tender.
storage: Soup keeps in the fridge up to 4 days. It thickens as it sits, so reheat it on the stove over medium-low heat with a splash of broth or milk. Freezing isn't recommended; the milk can turn grainy. Keep biscuits in a sealed bag at room temperature up to 2 days and rewarm them in a 350°F oven for 5 min.
